summary.prose: Building this fix adds a small approval queue to the chat host and routes every permission request through it. The adapters first mark whether a request ends the turn (claude) or waits inside it (codex and the control protocol); the panel then shows only the current request, relays or batches each decision, and starts one follow-up per finished batch with every approved tool allowed. The card gains a '1 of N' label that updates in place and reappears after the webview reloads.

tasks.title: Approval queue module
tasks.summary: A pure, vscode-free module (vscode-plugin/src/chat/approval-queue.ts) holding the ordered undecided requests {requestId, turnId, toolName?, command?, blockKind, resolution}, the current batch per originating turn {ended, decisions[]}, and the grant chain. Operations: enqueue, head (with position/total), decide(requestId, decision) refusing any id that is not the head, endTurn(turnId), batch completion check, clear() returning the undecided requests, grantChain (approved tool names, once each). No posting, no turns: the panel drives it.
acceptanceChecks: Requests keep arrival order; head() is the oldest undecided; decide() on any other id returns a refusal and changes nothing
A batch reports complete only after endTurn for its turn AND every request it raised is decided
The grant chain holds each approved tool-gate toolName once; dir-block approvals add nothing; clear() resets it and returns the undecided requests

tests.name: approval queue: requests are kept in arrival order and only the head is actionable; a decision for any other id is refused
approval queue: a batch is complete only when its turn has ended and every request is decided
approval queue: the grant chain accumulates approved tool names once each and resets on clear()

tasks.title: Mark approval requests with where they are answered
tasks.summary: Add optional resolution?: 'turn-ended' | 'in-turn' to the approval-request TurnEvent (stream-events.ts). In cli-adapter.ts the claude system/permission_denied branch sets 'turn-ended'; normalizeApprovalEvent (control-protocol and codex) sets 'in-turn'. No other field changes.

Existing adapter tests pass with only the added field

tasks.title: Route approval requests through the queue in the panel
tasks.summary: Replace pendingPerms with the t1 queue in chat-panel.ts. runTurn's TurnSink.onEvent and followLiveTurn's FollowSink.onEvent enqueue approval-requests (classifying blockKind as today) instead of posting them, and post only the head card with position/total; every other event is posted and persisted as today. A batch ends on its turn's terminal event (done/error) or a followed turn's onEnd. Stop (cancel-turn) records each undecided request as rejected and clears the queue; a chat switch or panel close drops it without outcome rows.
acceptanceChecks: A turn raising three approval-requests posts exactly one card (the first) with position 1 of 3
A followed turn's approval-requests also go through the queue
Stop records each undecided request as rejected and clears the queue; open-chat / new-chat / dispose drop it with no outcome rows
approval-request is still never written to the transcript

tasks.title: Decide only the head and relay in-turn decisions
tasks.summary: Rewrite the permission-decision handler's queue branch: a decision for a queued id that is not the head is ignored (debug log); the head's decision is recorded once (recordPermissionOutcome, in decision order); an in-turn request is relayed with decide(live.turnId, requestId, decision) (try/catch, a throw is logged and the queue still advances) before the next card is posted; a turn-ended request's decision joins its batch (an approved tool-gate joins the grant chain; an approved dir-block posts today's informational message). The next head is then posted. Ids not in the queue still fall through to decide() as today.
acceptanceChecks: A decision on a waiting card's id does nothing; the head's decision records exactly one outcome chip/row
The second card is posted only after the first is decided
An in-turn request (even one carrying a toolName) is relayed with decide() before the next card is posted and never starts a follow-up; a throwing decide() is logged and the queue advances
An id not in the queue still reaches the live adapter's decide()

tests.name: the second card is posted only after the first is decided; a decision on a waiting card's id does nothing
live-turn provider with two requests: decide() is called for the first before the second card is posted; no follow-up turn is started
an in-turn request that carries a toolName is relayed with decide(), not batched (routing by resolution)

tasks.title: One follow-up per completed turn-ended batch
tasks.summary: When a turn-ended batch is complete (its turn ended and every request decided), run exactly one follow-up via runTurn(prompt, grantChain, { suppressEcho: true }): one approved tool-gate uses today's exact prompt text ('Approved — run exactly this now: <command>' or the tool-name fallback); several use one combined prompt naming each approved action (exact command where captured) and each denied one; all denied (or only dir-blocks approved) posts an informational 'no action was approved' message and runs nothing. Requests the follow-up raises form the next batch; the grant chain carries over.
acceptanceChecks: Approving three turn-ended requests starts turns.start exactly once, after the last decision and the turn's end, with allowedTools = the three tools and a prompt naming the three actions
A denied request is named as denied in the combined follow-up; all denied runs no follow-up and posts the notice
A follow-up that is refused again forms a new batch whose follow-up carries the earlier grants
The existing single-request approve / deny / exact-command / tool-name / dir-block / suppressEcho tests pass unchanged

tests.name: approving all three starts exactly one follow-up turn, after the last decision and the turn's end, with allowedTools = all three tools and a prompt naming the three approved actions
no approval ever supersedes a running follow-up: turns.start is called once per batch
deny: a denied request gets a rejected chip, the next request is still asked, and the follow-up names it as denied; all denied -> no follow-up and an informational message
a follow-up that is refused again forms the next batch and its follow-up carries the previous batch's grants
single request: the existing approve/deny/exact-command/tool-name/dir-block/suppressEcho tests keep passing unchanged

tasks.title: A typed message clears the queue (denying in-turn requests first)
tasks.summary: On a user-typed submit-turn (not a follow-up), before the turn starts: answer every undecided in-turn request whose turn is still live with decide(live.turnId, requestId, 'deny'); then record each undecided request as rejected, clear the queue and reset the grant chain; then run the user's message as a normal turn.
acceptanceChecks: With a queued in-turn request, a typed message calls decide(turnId, requestId, 'deny') before the new turn starts
Every undecided request gets a rejected chip and the queue is empty
The next approval follow-up does not carry grants from before the typed message

tests.name: a user-typed message while requests are queued records each as rejected, clears the queue, resets the grant chain and runs as a normal turn
a live provider with a queued in-turn request, then the user types a message: decide(turnId, requestId, 'deny') is called before the new turn starts, and the request gets a rejected chip

tasks.title: Card position label, in-place update and re-post on reload
tasks.summary: Add a position label to the approval card in render-registry (shown as '1 of N' when total > 1; card unchanged without position/total). Add HostToWebview {type:'approval-position', requestId, position, total} in protocol.ts and a webview branch that finds .insrc-approval[data-request-id] and rewrites its label (unknown id ignored). The host posts a card at most once per requestId while shown and posts approval-position when the queue grows. postInitialState re-posts the head card with its position after session-restored (which clears the webview transcript), so exactly one head card exists afterwards.
acceptanceChecks: A card with position/total and total > 1 shows '1 of 3'; without them it renders exactly as before
A request joining the queue while the head is shown produces an approval-position message, not a second card
approval-position for an unknown id changes nothing
On 'ready' with a queued head, the head card is posted again, after session-restored, with its position, and exactly one card for it is posted
